pins.title: Family conversation cards for children who are still learning to read
pins.description: Can my child play before they can read a whole card? A grown-up can read a Secret Meeting Card aloud. Your child can answer, act it out on a DO turn or pass. Explore the 40-card printable set.

pins.title: Screen-free babysitting idea: leave a game the family already knows
pins.description: What can I leave for a carer to play after I head out? Print and cut a few Secret Meeting Cards beforehand. Your child can show the carer how to draw one and start a conversation together. See the 40-pack.

pins.title: Sea turtle movement game for kids: find a route using compass directions
pins.description: How can we practise directions outdoors? Mark a feeding ground and a nesting beach in a safe part of the park. Place three safe obstacles between them, then have a partner call compass directions along the route. Try the Sea Turtle Navigation Challenge.
pins.intended_board: Fun activities to do in Nature for kids

pins.title: Family litter survey: what turns up most often on your walk?
pins.description: Can children investigate litter without picking it up? On a safe walk with a grown-up, tally the paper, plastic and cans you see. Compare the counts and think of one way to prevent the most common item. Try the Litter Intelligence Mission.
pins.intended_board: Gaias Secret Agents protecting the Earth

pins.title: Outdoor science lesson: set an observation boundary before children start
pins.description: How can a group study nature while staying in sight? Agree on an observation boundary before heading out. Children can count visible plants, insects or birds from the path. An adult can sign up to access the free Teacher Starter Pack. Get the pack.
